newsitem.title: USA: Stocks end up, extend rebound for second day.
newsitem.headline: Stocks end up, extend rebound for second day.

text.p: Wall Street stocks, inspired by a drop in long-term interest rates and a stronger dollar, ended higher on Monday, extending their rebound to a second session.

The Dow Jones industrial average finished up 29.84 points, or 0.46 percent, at 6,555.91. Monday's rise followed a 49-point advance on Friday, which closed a week in which the blue chip average shed more than 214 points.
"Most of the world has been waiting and looking for some kind of a bounce, and this appears to be it," said Charles White, managing director at Avatar Associates.
In the broader market, advances beat declines 1,714 to 771 on active volume of 453 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

The Dow's rebound has failed to impress many Wall Street analysts. They cautioned that stocks could come under renewed pressure if long-term interest rates move higher or first-quarter corporate profit reports fail to meet expectations.
"We believe that this may be the type of rally that you're supposed to continue to sell into," said White.
Strength in the bond market, where investors reacted to a rise in the dollar against foreign currencies, led to bargain-hunting and short-covering in stocks, analysts said.

The 30-year Treasury bond was up 20/32 in late trading, or $6.25 on a $1,000 bond, and its yield dropped to 7.07 percent from 7.12 percent on Friday. The bond's price and yield move in opposite directions.
The recovery in stocks was led by technology shares, which were also at the forefront of the broader market's sell-off after they peaked in late January.
"This is a technical rally that could go on for a few days," Ricky Harrington, technical analyst at Interstate/Johnson Lane, said of Monday's stocks gain.
The Nasdaq composite, a barometer of the technology sector, showed its third-consecutive double-digit rise, jumping 14.62, or 1.18 percent, to 1,251.35.
Analysts said investors appeared to be buying technology stocks in anticipation of the first-quarter earnings report from Motorola Inc. Motorola gained 1/2 to end at 60-1/4.

After the close of trading, Motorola reported first-quarter profits of $325 million, or 53 cents a share, compared with $384 million, or 63 cents, in the year-ago period. But the latest results beat Wall Street analysts' forecast of 45 cents a share in profits.

The Motorola results were viewed as the first key piece of earnings news for Wall Street. Concerns that a slowing economy and the stronger dollar will hurt corporate profits have been factors in the recent sell-off.

"It's nice to see the market improve, but we've got to get through earnings first," said Guy Truicko, portfolio manager at Unity Management. The earnings period is "going to lead to some volatility over the next few weeks."
Retail brokerage Alex. Brown Inc. surged 9-7/8 to 63 on news it was merging with Bankers Trust New York Corp in a $1.7 billion stock swap. Bankers Trust ended down 2-3/4 at 79-1/2.

The proposed deal sent shares of other regional brokers leaping as traders viewed them as potential takeover targets. Legg Mason Inc. jumped 4 to 49, Morgan Keegan Inc. rose 2-1/8 to 19 and Piper Jaffray Cos gained 2 to 16-3/4.
In other trading, Nike Inc. fell 3-7/8 to 55-1/4 on heavy volume after Smith Barney cut its rating on the stock to neutral from outperform.
Allegheny Power Systems Inc. slipped 3/4 to 29 and DQE Inc., the parent of Duquesne Light Co., jumped 1-3/4 to 28-7/8 on news Allegheny would acquire DQE in a deal worth $2.6 billion.
Software giant Microsoft Corp. rose 1-11/16 to 95-7/8 after it said Sunday it was acquiring privately held WebTV Networks Inc. for cash and stock valued at about $425 million.

Rational Software Corp. tumbled 9-3/4 to 13-5/8 and Pure Atria Corp sank 7-3/4 to 10 after the two said they were merging and Pure Atria said it expected its first-quarter revenue and earnings would be below analysts' forecasts.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 4.23 points to 762.13. The American Stock Exchange index gained 3.71 to 560.44.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 2.66 to 400.68. The average share was up 27 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,272.992, up 59.031, or 0.82 percent.
